newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's CDU gains in Frankfurt local poll, TV says.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's CDU gains in Frankfurt local poll, TV says.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats recorded strong gains in local elections in the financial capital of Frankfurt on Sunday, a computer projection from the Forsa polling institute showed.

A projection broadcast by N-TV television about one hour after polls closed at 1700 GMT showed Kohl's CDU gaining 4.2 points in Frankfurt to 37.6 percent while the Social Democrats (SPD) slipped 1.7 points to 30.3 percent.
Kohl's CDU profited from the popularity of Frankfurt Mayor Petra Roth. The 52-year-old has led the city government in Germany's financial capital for the last two years.

In Frankfurt, the Greens gained 2.3 points from the last local election in 1993 to reach 16.3 percent, while the Free Democrats (FDP) were projected to receive 5.0 percent, just above their 4.4 percent in 1993. The far-right Republicans slipped to 5.9 percent from 9.3 percent.

The CDU also gained 1.3 points to achieve 31.6 percent in the southern Hesse city of Darmstadt, according to a computer projection by Hessischer Rundfunk television. The SPD lost 2.6 points to settle on 31.6 points.
A computer projection for the statewide results were expected by 1900 GMT.
